__doc__: THE DCGM EXPORTER SURFACE — one file, two independent producers, both asserted.
This repo has two things that emit DCGM metrics, and until this file existed
nothing compared them:
* on Kubernetes, run-ai/fake-gpu-operator's status-exporter (chart 0.0.59)
* outside it, compose/gpu-metrics-sim.py, which stands in for that exporter
so the GPU board can be developed on a laptop
The parity between them used to be prose in the compose simulator's header. A
chart bump that renamed a series or a label would fail the kind path loudly in
CI and let the compose path drift quietly, which is the wrong way round: the
compose path is the first command in the README.
WHY THE TWO SIDES ARE ASSERTED DIFFERENTLY — and an exact match on the cluster
side fails on day one, so this asymmetry is a decision rather than an oversight.
compose  (gpu-metrics-sim.py --selftest)   EXACT equality.
Nothing sits between the simulator and the assertion. It renders its own
exposition, so the series set and the label-key set must match this file
exactly — a name added here and not there is drift in either direction.
cluster  (verify.sh check 3b)              SUBSET.
Series arriving through Prometheus carry labels the exporter never
emitted — job, instance, namespace, pod, endpoint, service — because the
ServiceMonitor's target labels are attached at scrape time. Consumer-pod
labels arrive renamed to exported_*, since target labels win the
collision (docs/observability.md). So the assertion is: every series
named here is present, and every label key named here is present on it.
Extra labels are expected and are not drift.
THE THREE SERIES ARE THE WHOLE SURFACE, and that is a fact about the chart
rather than a choice. The status-exporter has no knob to emit more — no
container args, no metrics-config env var, nothing in `helm show values`.
DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_TEMP and DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_USAGE are synthesised from
utilisation by the recording rules in manifests/alerts/gpu-prometheusrule.yaml
and are therefore NOT part of this contract: they are derived, and verify.sh
check 4c is what asserts them. DCGM_FI_DEV_SM_CLOCK does not exist at all.
Adding a series here without adding it to BOTH producers fails the compose
selftest in the fast CI job within seconds. That is the intended way to find out.
